div.head: Grið 21
div.ab: Ac sume men syndan, þe for heora prytan ⁊ eac for gebyrdan forhogiað þæt hy hyran godcundan ealdran, swa swa hy sceoldan, gif hy riht woldan, ⁊ agynnað oft hyrwan þæt hy scoldan herian, ⁊ taliað þe wyrsan for heanan gebyrdan þa ðe heora yldran on worolde ne wurdan welige ne wlance þurh woroldglenge ne on lænan liffæce rance ne rice.

Ac sume men syndan, þe for heora prytan and eac for gebyrdan, forhogiað þæt hy hyran godcundan ealdran, swa swa hy sceoldan, gif hy riht woldan; and agynnað oft hyrwan þæt hy scoldan herian, and taliað þe wyrsan for heanan gebyrdan þa ðe heora yldran on worolde ne wurdan welige ne wlance þurh woroldglenge, ne on lænan liffæce rance ne rice.

Aber einige Menschen giebt es, die wegen ihres Stolzes und auch wegen Geburt[srang] verschmähen, geistlichen Oberen so zu gehorchen, wie sie, wenn sie Rechtes erstreben würden, müssten, und oft [das] zu schmähen wagen, was sie preisen sollten, und diejenigen wegen [deren] niederer Geburt für um so geringer achten, deren Voreltern im Weltlichen nicht wohlhabend, noch hervorragend durch weltlichen Pomp, noch in [dieser] vergänglichen Lebensspanne vornehm noch reich wurden.

But there are some people who, because of their pride and also because of [rank of] birth, scorn to obey spiritual superiors as they would have to if they strove after what is right, and often dare to revile [what] they ought to praise, and think the less of those, because of [their] low birth, whose forebears in worldly affairs did not become wealthy, nor distinguished by worldly pomp, nor noble or rich in [this] transitory span of life.

But there are some who, because of their pride and also their birth, refuse to heed their spiritual betters, just as they ought to do if they desired virtue; and they often begin to blame what they should praise, and judge those to be inferior because of their humble birth whose ancestors were not in this world either wealthy or made proud through their worldly finery, or in this transitory life prosperous or powerful.
